reason: The quotation is exact and the edition claim is false. I downloaded the named file, Project Gutenberg 1322, and read the poem at line 8906. It is eight lines and the last three stand character for character as the card gives them, with the elisions wander'd and Look'd, the comma after time to time, and the closing full stop. The cluster heading BOOK XX. BY THE ROADSIDE sits at line 8682 and the next heading, BOOK XXI. DRUM-TAPS, at line 9174, so the poem does fall under Book XX in that file. But the evidence then names the edition as the 1891 to 1892 deathbed edition, and that file is not it. Two structural tells settle it. First, the file numbers Sands at Seventy as BOOK XXXIV and Good-Bye My Fancy as BOOK XXXV, continuing the sequence; in the 1891 to 1892 volume those are the First and Second Annexes, tacked on after the main sequence and not numbered into it. Second, the file contains no A Backward Glance o'er Travel'd Roads at all, and the deathbed volume carries that essay. Project Gutenberg 1322 gives no edition statement anywhere in its front matter, which I checked, so nothing the verifier read supported the 1891 to 1892 claim; it was asserted on top of a text that contradicts it. The Book numbering is the apparatus of the posthumous David McKay arrangement, so the card as it stands pairs a locator from one printing with the name of another. That is a confident false citation of exactly the kind the standard forbids, and it is worse than the page range the verifier honourably dropped from the Neruda card, because here the reader is told which edition was consulted. The line itself is sound and should ship with the edition claim removed: the wording is Whitman's own from Drum-Taps in 1865 and is unchanged through the 1891 to 1892 printing, and By the Roadside is the cluster in every arrangement. Everything else clears: shipped.js returns no match, no near match, Whitman at 0 of 3, not banned; in scope and publishable; perfect on silence for six in the morning; Poetry is the form; the corrected source line leads with the name, carries no dash, and runs 107 characters. The note should say that Book XX is the numbering of the posthumous David McKay arrangement read on Project Gutenberg and not a division of Whitman's own edition.
